task_title: Design end-to-end architectures (input → processing → output → feedback loops)
title: $6,500 paid with no check: close the loop around the decision step
stem: Harbour Mutual's claims pipeline sends each claim and its policy to Claude, which returns a decision that the pipeline executes. Last week it paid a $6,500 claim, above the agent's $5,000 payout authority, and the team has no record of which decisions adjusters later reversed. Which change to the end-to-end architecture best addresses both problems?

options.A: Add the $5,000 payout authority and the excess rule to the system prompt with worked examples, so that Claude refers large claims to an adjuster on its own initiative.
options.B: Validate each decision in code against the payout rules, retry once with the errors, route anything still failing to an adjuster, and store each adjuster decision as a labelled eval case.
options.C: Log every request and response to the observability store, and review a weekly sample of 50 decisions with the adjusters to agree the prompt changes for each release of the claims pipeline.
options.D: Switch the decision step to a larger model with extended thinking, since the payout shows that the current model's reasoning about policy limits is not reliable enough.

why: The pipeline is open loop: whatever the model returns is executed, and nothing is learned. Closing the loop keeps the same model and prompt and adds stages around the call: checks before it, a validator in code after it (coverage, quote minus excess, payout authority), one repair retry for fixable errors (seconds), an action gate that sends rule breaks to a person and fails closed (minutes), and a feedback path that saves every adjuster decision as a labelled eval case for the next change to be tested against (days).

wrong.A: A prompt makes the referral more likely, but when it fails the decision still executes unchecked, and no feedback is captured.
wrong.C: Logging and sampling find problems after the money has gone; nothing stops a bad payout before it executes.
wrong.D: A larger model is still probabilistic and still unchecked, and the pipeline would still learn nothing from adjuster decisions.

fix: Wrap the decision step: rules validated in code, one repair retry, an action gate to an adjuster, and adjuster decisions saved as eval cases.
see: The validator holds CLM-7815 for the adjuster, valid payouts still go through, and the adjuster's decision becomes an eval case.
explain: In Phase 1 every decision executes: CLM-7815 is approved for $6,500 and paid, above the $5,000 authority, and nothing is recorded. In Phase 2 the same decision step runs inside a closed loop. Input checks confirm the claimant is the policyholder and the policy is active. An output validator in code checks each decision against the payout rules; a wrong amount would get one retry with the errors. CLM-7815 breaks the authority rule, so the action gate sends it to an adjuster instead of executing it. The adjuster's decision, with the model's proposal beside it, is saved as a labelled eval case that the next prompt or model change must pass.
exam_tip: When a stem says a system acts on model output and nothing is learned from it, choose the answer that checks the output in code before acting, routes failures to a person, and feeds those decisions back as test cases.
headline: Validate, gate, and turn every review into a test.

concepts.b: Input, processing and output are what you demo. The feedback stage (traces, human decisions, outcomes) is what lets the system improve, and it is what you operate.
Hard rules such as coverage, quote minus excess and payout authority are checked by code on every decision, independently of the model that produced it.
If the validator fails, errors or cannot decide, the action gate sends the case to a person. It never executes by default.
Repair one output (seconds), human review of risky cases (minutes), and offline improvement where failures become eval cases that gate the next change (days).
